hook: Your phone buzzes on the desk and your stomach tightens before you even read it, because the last ten buzzes were group-chat drama. Nothing about a buzz is upsetting by itself. You learned that reaction by pairing: the buzz kept arriving right before something that already upset you. That is classical conditioning, and it explains fears, cravings, and even why one bad meal can put you off a food for years.

prereq.q: A study measures "stress" as the number of times a person checks their phone in ten minutes. What is that?
prereq.why: It says exactly how the study measures the variable, which is an operational definition.

options: Traits that helped ancestors survive and reproduce become more common
Animals change their genes on purpose to survive
Every trait is learned from parents after birth
Traits that appear late in life are always passed on
prereq.why: Natural selection: heritable traits that helped survival and reproduction become more common over generations. That idea explains biological preparedness in this topic.

figure.caption: Before, during and after: the tone becomes a conditioned stimulus because it predicts food.

chain.cause: A neutral stimulus (a tone) comes just before an unconditioned stimulus (food) again and again
chain.effect: the tone starts to predict the food (acquisition)
the tone alone triggers salivation: it is a conditioned stimulus and the salivation is a conditioned response

chain.cause: The tone keeps sounding without food

chain.effect: the response can return for a while (spontaneous recovery), so the learning was suppressed, not erased

ideas: Find the UCS first: the thing that causes a response with no learning (food, a shot, a loud noise). Its automatic response is the UCR.
The CS is the once-neutral stimulus that came before the UCS. The learned reaction to it is the CR. The UCR and CR are often the same movement, triggered by different things.
Extinction weakens a CR when the CS comes without the UCS; spontaneous recovery brings it back after a rest. Generalization spreads a CR to similar stimuli; discrimination limits it.
Taste aversion can form after one pairing with hours between taste and illness, an example of biological preparedness. Habituation, a fading response to a repeated stimulus, needs no pairing at all.

misconception.wrong: Extinction means the animal has forgotten the conditioned stimulus.
misconception.right: Extinction suppresses the conditioned response, but the learning survives: after a rest the response can return (spontaneous recovery), and it is relearned faster than it was first learned.

summary: Classical conditioning is learning by association. A neutral stimulus that comes just before an unconditioned stimulus becomes a conditioned stimulus that triggers a conditioned response. Extinction weakens that response, spontaneous recovery shows the learning is still there, generalization spreads it and discrimination narrows it. Biology sets limits: some links, such as taste with illness, form after one pairing.
